notes: v1.14.545 — LEGACY-RETIRE STAGE 6.1: THE FIRST BORROWED ORGAN IS DECOUPLED. #issue-page is now AUTHORED inside #wk-issues instead of being re-parented there from pg-twin at boot. redesign_homeIssues and its DOMContentLoaded registration are deleted — the first of the eight re-homes to go — and the pg-twin shell goes with them. The div keeps its id and inline padding verbatim, because issue_renderList and issue_pageOpen resolve it with getElementById: the node's identity is the contract, not its position. ⛔ Three edits had to land in ONE ship: author the markup while the re-home still runs and the node is merely moved from where it already is; delete the re-home first and the surface is empty until the markup lands. ⚠ VISIBLE UNDER ?legacy=1: the legacy house LOSES the Issue Log. An organ is a single node, so decoupling it necessarily takes it out of one house — this is inherent to Stage 6 and will repeat for the seven organs that follow. The legacy NERVE tile is removed with it rather than left as a dead tap into a deleted page (Contract 14), and the three .qa-nerve CSS rules it orphaned go too. The legacy 'twin' branch in showPage is removed; the redesign's upstream redirect to showWorkTab('issues') STAYS, so a device holding saved nav state p:'twin' still restores to the right surface. Guarded by test/e2e/45-borrowed-organs.spec.js, whose organ-4 assertion fails loudly if #wk-issues is ever empty again.
